subject.title: [Feature]: Support arbitrary workspace files in bootstrap context injection

question: Should OpenClaw accept explicitly configured custom-basename files in `bootstrap-extra-files` as a core startup-context contract, or keep the hook limited to recognized workspace bootstrap filenames?
rationale: This is a product and security-boundary choice because it changes which configured workspace files can enter deterministic system-prompt context before a session starts.

options.title: Approve Guarded Custom Files
options.body: Allow explicitly configured custom-basename files through the existing hook after the linked PR or a replacement preserves path guards, budgets, session filtering, and documentation.

options.title: Keep Recognized Basenames
options.body: Reject arbitrary bootstrap-file injection and keep custom context routed through existing first-class workspace files or a narrower filename-specific proposal.

options.title: Defer To Context API Design
options.body: Leave the current allowlist intact and handle arbitrary context injection in a broader context or capability-discovery design.

recommendation.title: Approve Guarded Custom Files
recommendation.body: Allow explicitly configured custom-basename files through the existing hook after the linked PR or a replacement preserves path guards, budgets, session filtering, and documentation.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-line ownership and timeline mention make `vincentkoc` the best available routing candidate for deciding the loader/hook contract.
